newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ORIOLES PUT ALOMAR ON 15-DAY DISABLED LIST.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ORIOLES PUT ALOMAR ON 15-DAY DISABLED LIST.

text.p: The Baltimore Orioles put eight-time All-Star second baseman Roberto Alomar on the 15-day disabled list with a pulled right groin on Wednesday.
Alomar left Tuesday night's game against Texas in the sixth inning due to the injury.
"When I went out there, he (Alomar) said he heard it pop," said Orioles manager Davey Johnson after Tuesday's 5-4 win.
Alomar is hitting .298 with 10 homers and 43 RBI in his second season with the Orioles.
He signed a three-year, $18 million contract with Baltimore after the 1995 season and batted .328 with 22 home runs, 94 RBI and a club-record 141 runs scored last year.

Alomar's image suffered severe damage last year when he spit in the face of umpire John Hirschbeck while arguing a called third strike in the final weekend of the regular season. He was suspended for the first five games of the 1997 season for the incident.
Alomar established himself as one of baseball's top all-around players in his five seasons with Toronto, helping the Blue Jays win back-to-back World Series titles in 1992 and 1993.
Designated hitter Harold Baines, who was acquired from the Chicago White Sox on Tuesday, is taking Alomar's spot on the roster.
